body: The CPUs the kernel lists as performance cores in /sys/devices/cpu_core/cpus (0-15 on this i9-13900K); with no such list, any CPU. Instead: Pin to the 4 highest-frequency CPUs as the recommendation's wording read.
rests_on: Escalation 5c777a6a's recommendation described the performance cores as 'the CPUs with the highest maximum frequency', but cpuinfo_max_freq here has three classes: 4 CPUs at 5.8 GHz (two favored cores), 12 at 5.5 GHz and 16 at 4.3 GHz, so that wording names only the favored cores, while the kernel's cpu_core list is 0-15 and cpu_atom is 16-31. The evidence the developer ruled on was measured on 0-15 (taskset -c 0-15: bar_005_ passed 3 of 3 at load 27-31). The developer was told of the difference after answering ('The code uses the kernel's performance-core list, CPUs 0-15 ... If you want only the 5.8 GHz cores instead, say so') and replied 'ok' at 11:47; the prompt for escalation b3fc52a5 said 'Treat this ok as your confirmation of the 16-core set (CPUs 0-15) for the frame check', answered 'ok' (answer 1eff02fb, 14:53). The adversary's acceptance 08eba8b3 finding 2 asks for that confirmation on record. 050a6fb5 implements the kernel list.
title: Which CPUs are the performance cores that the frame-budget measurement runs on under the developer's answer to escalation 5c777a6a?

subject: The z_index_tests crash was found to be a host fault, not the code: its core dump (1250999, 2026-09-22 19:01) crashed in ld.so during relocation before main, so no test code ran, and 15,773 runs of the binary beside cargo test --workspace were clean. The gates now tell such faults from failures: a compiler, rustdoc, clippy-driver or linker killed by a signal, under a wrapper too, or a doc-test failed only by one, is recorded unverified, not failed (c1cdff23, a7806288, 6ba6be59, 04a87d73, e6ab472d, 91d24714, 57757d80), and the gates prove the test run happened (src/gate_proof.rs). On the adversary's findings the workspace gates, dangling-paths, widget-bar, charts-goldens and assertion-audit mechanisms were hardened, and tests that assumed an idle machine were fixed. Captured for later: gate-doctest-outcome-lines, test-timing-sweep, doc-gate-rustdoc-json.

The frame-budget group in scripts/cairn/charts_contract.py pins itself (os.sched_setaffinity, inherited by cargo and the test) to the CPUs the kernel lists in /sys/devices/cpu_core/cpus, intersected with the allowed CPUs, and prints the CPUs it used; with no such list it changes nothing (050a6fb5). With CPUs 10-11 taken offline for a hardware test, it followed the kernel's list 0-9,12-15.

body: tests/api_component_expansion.rs recursive_expansion_fails_with_a_bounded_error overflows the 2 MB test-thread stack when the crate is built with the embedded-terminal feature (cargo test --features embedded-terminal --test api_component_expansion, 2026-09-23, reproduced on 87c06d49 with no working changes). The component runtime bounds expansion at depth 128 (src/component/runtime.rs) and each level's debug-build frame in expand is large enough that 128 levels fill the stack; with default features it passes. Either lower the bound, shrink expand's frame (move the instance creation into a separate function), or run expansion on a thread with a known stack. Not renderer work.

body: An animation update pass that another thread began before a hook owner closes can still set one value after close() returns. update_animations delivers each task outside the registry lock; the stagger, spring and keyframe update closures check the owner's generation and then set the value without a lock that cancel_owned_work takes (src/hooks/animation.rs, schedule_item and the other update closures), so a pass already past the check sets the item once more. Found while fixing the rac_001 stagger flake on 2026-09-23; the tests now wait for such a pass, the library does not. Close the window without holding a lock across ThreadSafeSignal::set, whose subscribers may start or cancel animations: for example re-check the generation after setting and restore, or have cancel wait for an in-flight pass of that owner. Not renderer work.

body: The timer and clipboard hooks check their hook owner's liveness by upgrading a Weak<HookResources>, as the animation owners did before cb91d5e5. HookTimer::restart (src/hooks/timer.rs) upgrades it while holding the timer's state lock, and lines 186, 284 and 346 upgrade it on other paths; the clipboard hook's copy and paste callbacks (src/hooks/clipboard.rs:215, 233) do the same. If another thread drops the last Hooks clone while one of these holds the upgraded reference, dropping it runs HookResources::close on that thread, and the timer's cleanup may then wait for the lock the thread holds. Switch them to Liveness (Hooks::liveness), and add a test like animation's dropping_the_last_hooks_during_update_passes_never_hangs that hangs with the Weak upgrade. local_hooks.rs already defers dropping upgraded owners until after its borrow. Found by the animation-close-inflight-pass adversary (report 61b74425, finding 1), which reproduced the hang for animations only.

body: The SuprTUI import keeps modules reactive-tui never calls: audio, clipboard, layout, sys, term, term_embedded and text (about 200 KB with their tests). The application uses ansi, buffer, render, uni and blit, and link and media only through buffer. term::Capabilities has ten flags nothing ever sets (kitty_graphics, rgb, ansi256, sgr_pixels, explicit_width, scaled_text, sixel, sync, notifications, remote) and duplicates the application's own probe in src/core/capabilities.rs. crates/reactive-tui-suprtui/UPSTREAM.md keeps the whole import on purpose so renderer changes can be checked against upstream, so pruning reverses a recorded choice. Decide per module: delete it and its tests, or make it the application's implementation (for example one capability probe instead of two). Found while documenting the crate's public items on 2026-09-23.

body: A pie or donut label's leader can end on a neighbouring slice instead of its own (acceptance 0fffbe6d finding 1, medium; breaks CHT-015's falsifier 'a placed label has no leader line to its slice'). On an 80x24 pie of [1,1,1,1,1,20,1,1] at the default label_gap, p0's leader runs along row 0 to (0,49), next to p1's chart-2 cells (0,46)-(0,48); p0's own cells on that row end at (0,44), and p1 has no label, so p0 reads as p1's. The reviewer's sweep found it in 192 of 440 configurations (pie and donut, every size and gap), on the top and bottom rows. Cause: edge() in place_labels (src/widgets/display/charts/live/canvas/pie.rs) starts the leader past the outermost painted cell on the anchor row, whichever slice owns it. Fix: start the leader at a cell the label's own slice owns (MaskCanvas::owner_at), on a row where that slice is outermost on the label's side, and leave the label out when no such row exists; make cht_015's leader walk require the end cell to be the label's own slice. Closed by the developer's ok on escalation 36c507fd.

body: Show the slices whose labels were left out first, then the labelled slices in slice order while they fit, keeping slice order along the legend Instead: Keep the first-slices legend and capture the CHT-015 and CHT-024 conflict as a backlog item, which leaves a slice named nowhere on crowded medium pies until then; or revise CHT-024 so a medium legend may wrap, which changes an Agreed requirement and every chart's layout.
rests_on: CHT-015 says 'omitting a label that cannot be placed without overlapping another while keeping its slice in the legend'; CHT-024 gives the medium class a 'single-row legend'. canvas.rs:439-466 reserves the legend rectangle from every entry before pie() runs and draws it after, and legend.rs:103 (draw_flowed) stops at the first entry that does not fit, so a truncated legend drops the last slices whatever the face shows. Adversary report ff366b56 finding 1: an 80x24 pie with a Top legend, seven 12-character names and values [30, 20, 15, 12, 10, 10, 3] draws five legend entries while the seventh slice's label is left out, so that slice is named nowhere. Preferring unlabelled slices changes only which entries a full legend draws, not its size or the plot area, and keeps both requirements whenever the unlabelled slices fit in the legend.
title: When a pie or donut label is left out and the legend cannot show every slice (a medium legend is one row), which slices should the legend show?
wrong_if: A reader who expects a full legend to list slices from the first sees it skip some labelled slices; those slices are still named by their labels on the chart, so no slice becomes unnamed, and the choice is one function to revert.

body: Pie and donut labels are left out while free rows remain (acceptance 0fffbe6d finding 2, low; conflicts with CHT-015's text, which allows omitting only a label that cannot be placed without overlapping another). The 80x24 pie of [1,1,1,1,1,20,1,1] at the default gap places 6 of 8 labels: p1 and p7 are dropped while rows 6-22 on the right and 1-22 on the left are free; across the reviewer's sweep 246 of 3880 labels were left out, and every crowded set at 80x24, 81x25 and 120x30 placed only 6 or 7 of 8. Cause: leader() always lays its horizontal run on the label's anchor row, and there an earlier label's leader already runs. Fix: let a leader leave the circle on another row where its slice is outermost, and raise cht_015's placed-label floor (now 3 of 8). Closed by the developer's ok on escalation 36c507fd.

body: DebugBackend lays out and paints on the thread that runs the app, so drawing the deepest tree expansion accepts (128 levels) needs about 1.8 MiB of that thread's stack in a debug build (1856 KiB measured with default features, 2110 KiB with embedded-terminal, by the resident size of a fresh 48 MiB thread stack after the run). A test that does this on a 2 MiB test thread with embedded-terminal overflows and aborts the test run. The peak is taffy's flexbox recursion (compute_preliminary 2.6 KiB, determine_flex_base_size 3.1 KiB and more per level at opt-level 0), not reactive-tui's own frames: moving element_to_paintspec's per-node work out of its recursive collect (7.5 KiB to 440 B per level) left the peak unchanged. Options: lay out and paint DebugBackend frames on a worker thread with its own stack, as SuprTuiBackend does; or reduce the layout's per-level stack. Found by the expansion-depth-stack acceptance 25438088, finding 1; the manual now states the limit.

body: Check two decisions the test-timing-sweep commitment (ca57e784) made without asking. Both go past a literal reading of its rule that a timing under test stays as it is. (1) src/hooks/timer.rs: test_debounced_function's debounce delay went from 10 ms to 500 ms, and test_throttled_function's throttle interval from 50 ms to 500 ms; the sleeps after them went from 20 ms and 60 ms to 600 ms. The tests make their calls and the cancel, or the rapid second and third calls, inside that delay, and on a busy machine 10 ms and 50 ms can pass before the next call runs, so the old tests could fail with no defect. The behavior tested is the same. (2) tests/embedded_terminal.rs emb_005_delayed_output_exit_and_idle_shutdown_are_observable: the bound on idle.shutdown() went from 2 s to 10 s. EmbeddedSession::shutdown has no timeout of its own, so the bound only has to tell killing the fixture child ('exec sleep 30') at once from waiting out its 30 s; tests/api_clipboard.rs (which fixture) and tests/api_widget_behavior/dialog_http.rs (removal) already use 10 s against a 30 s fixture. Decide for each: keep it, or restore the original value and make the test hold on a busy machine another way, for example a test clock the timer hooks can take.
